name: terminal
description: Execute shell commands in the user sandbox. IMPORTANT: this sandbox is EMPTY and ISOLATED by default — it does NOT contain files produced by other skills (file_generation, html_preview, image_generation, etc all write to separate Mongo-backed storage, never to this filesystem) and it does NOT contain OADSON's own skill code (skills are not importable Python modules — 'import html_preview' or similar will always fail with ModuleNotFoundError, there is no such package). If a file from an earlier step needs to be edited or read here, you must first write/download it INTO this sandbox yourself (e.g. via curl/wget from its download_url, or via the workspace skill) — never assume it already exists here. NEVER curl/wget this app's own /files/serve/... URLs (oadson-v3.onrender.com or similar) to pull a file into the sandbox — on this single-worker instance that deadlocks the server (the worker handling your request is the only one that could answer that request, so it hangs until timeout with 0 bytes transferred). Use document_reader's fetch_upload action instead for any file with a download_url. NEVER use bare absolute paths like '/', '/*', or '/tmp/...', and never use '..' to escape upward — these are always outside the sandbox and always blocked; use relative paths only (e.g. 'ls repos/' not 'ls /*' or 'ls ..'), and don't retry the same blocked path a second time expecting a different result — if blocked once, switch to a relative path immediately. Do not import third-party libraries in one-off Python (e.g. 'import fitz' for PDFs) unless you've confirmed they're installed — document_reader already handles PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX reading and is almost always the right tool instead. For cloning a repo + installing + zipping: use action=clone_install_zip with repo=owner/name — do NOT write chained cd && npm install && zip commands manually, they break. For downloading packages: use action=download_packages. For simple commands: use query. Timeout auto-extends to 180s for package manager commands (npm, pip, yarn, cargo, etc).

query.description: A single shell command or && -chained compound command. For multiple separate commands, prefer 'script' instead to save steps.

script.description: A multi-line shell script — use this to batch multiple operations into ONE step instead of calling terminal repeatedly. Each line is a separate command. All lines run together in one subprocess and return combined stdout/stderr. Example: 'ls repos/x/\ncat repos/x/main.py\npython3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open(\"repos/x/main.py\").read())"'. PREFER this over multiple terminal calls.

action.description: 'run_code': run a source-code snippet in a specific language (see language/code/filename/stdin params) — writes to a real file first, avoids shell-escaping issues with raw code. 'run' (default): execute shell command. 'download_packages': download pip/npm/yarn/cargo packages and zip them. 'clone_install_zip': clone a GitHub repo, run install, and zip it — all in one step. Use clone_install_zip instead of chaining cd && npm install && zip manually.

packages.description: Package names for download_packages action. e.g. ["requests", "numpy"]

manager.description: Package manager for download_packages. Default: pip.

output_name.description: Output zip filename for download_packages. Default: packages.zip

include_modules.description: For clone_install_zip: include node_modules in zip. Default false (excluded to keep zip small).

install_flags.description: Extra flags for install command e.g. --production

language.description: For action=run_code. Language of the snippet. Supported here, CONFIRMED present in the sandbox: python, javascript (node), typescript (via npx tsx, first run may be slower while it installs), bash. java runtime exists but the COMPILER (javac) does not — java source will return a clear error rather than run; only Python/JS/TS/bash actually execute. Do not assume other languages (ruby, go, rust, php, etc) are installed — use action='run' with 'which <interpreter>' first to check before trying.

code.description: For action=run_code. The full source code to run.

filename.description: For action=run_code. Optional filename to save the snippet as (extension auto-added if missing). Default: snippet.<ext>.

stdin.description: For action=run_code. Optional input to feed the program's stdin.
